findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive, trivially bypassed
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does an exact match (`where(email: email).first`) against the value supplied by the signup form. Email addresses are not normalized/downcased before User validation (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` verbatim and there is no downcasing callback), so a user whose address `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked can sign up with `Bad@Spamclub.com` and pass validation. The stored block rows are also inserted verbatim, so a mixed-case row would never match a lowercase signup. The lookup should normalize both sides (e.g. `Email.downcase`) and the column/index should store normalized values.

findings.title: Validator performs DB writes, so match statistics are double-counted
findings.body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which mutates and saves the BlockedEmail row (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`). Because this happens inside validation, every call to `valid?`/`save` writes. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, so a single signup attempt runs the validation twice and inflates `match_count` by 2; any other code path that validates a user with a changed email also silently bumps the counter. Side-effect-free validation plus an explicit statistics update (or an idempotent guard) is needed, otherwise the match statistics are unreliable.

findings.title: Non-atomic increment of match_count loses updates
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write across two statements. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address (the common case for spam waves) will read the same value and overwrite each other, so `match_count` under-reports. Use an atomic update (`increment!`/`update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`). Additionally `record.save` re-runs the uniqueness validation (extra query) and silently returns false if the record is invalid, so a failed statistics update goes unnoticed.

findings.title: action_type is NOT NULL with no database default
findings.body: `action_type` is declared `null: false` but has no default; the only default comes from the model's `before_validation :set_defaults`. Any insert that bypasses the model (bulk import of blocked addresses via SQL/COPY, which the spec comments explicitly anticipate, or `insert_all`-style code) will fail with a not-null violation. Add `default: 0` (block) to the column so the DB and model agree.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared across instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` creates a single array on the class prototype; every instance of CreateAccountController mutates the same array via `pushObject`. If the controller is ever instantiated more than once (or the app is reset in tests), rejected emails leak between instances and are never cleared, so a previously rejected address stays permanently marked invalid for the page lifetime. Initialize it per-instance in `init` (or reset it when the modal is shown).
